tao: paging: PAGERDUTY gpu-decode-oom firing for stream-prod-eu-1. multiple decode pods restarting, lots of 137/oom-kill + CUDA errors. observed large spike in token counts from a subset of streaming requests. logs attached below. anyone oncall pls ack? :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created: ID INC-1801234560 - Severity: P0. PagerDuty link: https://pd.example/INC-1801234560. Escalation: oncall @maria.

maria: on it. taking pager. tao can you paste the error snippet and any recent deploys?

tao: no deploys in last hour. past 10m of logs: ```
[stream-decode-0] runtime.ERROR: CUDA error: out of memory (driver api) at kernel LaunchTensor...
[stream-decode-0] pid=1123 SIGKILL (OOM)
[stream-decode-1] kv_cache.size=124MiB -> growing to 3.1GiB in 45s for conn=acme-analytics/stream-req-789
[ingress] request id=xx-yyy tokens_accumulated=512000 user_agent=internal-retry-middleware
```

james: interesting - token_accumulated ~512k is huge. looks like a client kept appending during a retry loop. do we have request-level max_tokens enforcement in the kernel?

samantha: runtime insight - we validate max_tokens on the gateway layer but streaming clients sometimes set header `X-Stream-Append: true` and middleware can re-open streams without re-checking quota. KV growth looks unbounded. kernel logs show `cuMemAlloc` failures at ~6.8GB which then cascaded to OOM and container restart.

leo: support flagging: customer acme-analytics reported partial drops to their engineers ~5m ago. ticket created: TICK-6543. I'll DM them that we're investigating and to temporarily stop streaming retries.

maria: mitigation plan (short):
- enable emergency feature-flag: `enforce-stream-max-tokens=true` across ingress in eu region (tao)
- cordon and drain the 3 flapping decode pods, restart with container limits lowered (james)
- route 10% of traffic to fallback small-lm-int8 pool to reduce pressure (samantha)
- add iptables rule to drop requests with tokens_accumulated > 100k at edge for 10m (tao)

tao: doing the FF toggle now. curl -X POST https://config-console/flags -d '{"flag":"enforce-stream-max-tokens","value":true,"region":"eu"}' -> 200 OK. pushing rule: `kubectl exec edge-plt -- iptables -A RAW -m string --string "tokens_accumulated=" --algo bm -j DROP` (patched quickly, will replace with proper nginx lua check).

oncall-bot: @maria acknowledged. Rolling restart job queued for stream-decode-group in eu: job id restart-1801234560.

james: draining pods now: `kubectl drain pod/stream-decode-0 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> pod evicted, new pod started on node g4dn-xlarge-12. monitoring.

samantha: firing a temporary autoscale: increase dedicated fallback pool by +4 nodes, and enable immediate routing. `redwoodctl routes update --cluster eu --route streaming --fallback small-lm-int8 --weight 10` -> accepted.

tao: observing request drops drop by ~70% after iptables rule + FF. memory pressure decreasing on remaining decode pods.

leo: customer update sent: "We've applied emergency throttles and routed a portion of traffic to a fallback model. You may see partial request drops for ~10m while we stabilize; no data was exposed. We'll follow up with timeline and RCA."

maria: quick note: reason for event = unbounded KV growth from repeated append/resume streams combined with missing revalidation on retries. kernel-level cuMemAlloc then fails, container restarted -> user-visible drops.

james: root cause hypothesis: client-side retry loop + missing server-side guard for accumulated tokens. fix = enforce token ceiling on ingress for all streaming sessions + per-session KV cap and early abort. also add a soft-circuit breaker when a session's KV exceeds 200MB.

samantha: hotfix checklist for postmortem:
- prod patch: require `max_tokens` param or default cap of 64k for streaming.
- runtime: add per-session KV accounting and evict/deny when > 200MB.
- infra: add node-level alert for rapid KV growth (rate of change)
- deprecate legacy retry middleware path that re-opens streams without handshake.

maria: on-call handoff: I'm keeping eyes for 10m then handing to james for overnight followup. current status: severity reduced to P1, customer impact limited to partial drops for acme-analytics and a handful of internal test streams.

incident-bot: Severity updated to P1. Incident state: Contained. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/incidents/INC-1801234560

tao: note: we restarted 6 pods total across two nodes; 2 pods failed health after restart -> those are still on older kernel driver 515.43. james can you patch node driver to 515.65?

james: scheduling kernel/driver upgrade on those nodes now. will coordinate with infra windows.

leo: support follow-up: setting expectation with customer for full RCA in 48h and offering a hand-hold migration for their streaming SDK to our newer client libs that enforce single-stream semantics.

maria: thanks everyone. Handoff: james owns the postmortem + driver roll, samantha owns runtime changes, tao owns ingress rule + flag cleanup, leo owns customer comms + ticket. I'll update the incident doc and ping the oncall rotation.

samantha: quick todo already added to backlog: add unit tests around stream resume and retry behavior.

maria: handing off now -> @james you're owner. good job team. :pray:
